facts.fact: Minutes of the project's consultations with councils, annexed to the plan, record a M'mbelwa district executive member on 11 July 2024 speaking of the internet the Digital Malawi Project provided to the councils as very slow and unreliable, which the project team accepted, and a regional meeting of June 2024 recording that Kasungu has 5MB on the Boma network, that the project bought Wi-Fi adapters so council desktops could receive the Wi-Fi 6 provided, and that the Department of E-Government can raise a council's bandwidth on request.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

facts.fact: The consultation minutes of June and July 2024 record council officers logging in to the Boma network internet with passwords and meeting a 50MB limit on file attachments, some sites requiring a government email or ID to reach the internet, and councils still waiting for government email accounts: Dedza District Council was promised them by 1 July 2024 and Lilongwe City Council had supplied staff details long before with nothing done.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

facts.fact: The consultation minutes of June and July 2024 speak of internet provided to the councils by the Digital Malawi Project and name Kasungu as on the Boma network, record on 25 June 2024 that Dowa was yet to be connected under that project and that some sites from it were not working, and give no count of councils connected against the 35 district, municipal and city councils the plan says exist.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

facts.fact: The consultation minutes of June and July 2024 say the Department of E-Government manages the councils' internet on the government network, setting each institution's bandwidth and attachment limits and issuing government email, and that it is short of technical staff to support all 35 local councils promptly.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

facts.fact: The consultation minutes of June and July 2024 say the councils' internet was provided by the Digital Malawi Project and that its successor has a ten-year agreement with contractors to provide and maintain the service, with the government to take it into its budget through E-Government once World Bank funding ends; a council participant said on 25 June 2024 that council ICT offices get no funding to buy data bundles or small equipment.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study of the four city councils, researched to early 2022, reports the revenue system vendors saying the cities chose cloud-based systems and so had to secure enough internet bandwidth at their local government offices, that some had to upgrade their connectivity when the systems were rolled out, and that Blantyre took seven months to install bandwidth sufficient for its system.
facts.system: City councils' office internet for cloud-based Revenue Management Systems

facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study says staff of the Blantyre, Lilongwe, Mzuzu and Zomba city councils work in cloud-based Revenue Management Systems introduced from 2017, generating, authorising and printing demand notices and business licences online and watching market point-of-sale devices in real time, with depth varying by city and Lilongwe's use described as low; none had been integrated with the local IFMIS or the banks by the time of the research in early 2022.
facts.system: Revenue Management Systems of the four city councils

facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study describes cloud-based revenue systems, and the office internet they need, at four local governments, the city councils of Blantyre, Lilongwe, Mzuzu and Zomba, of the 35 local governments it counts (28 district, 4 city and 3 municipal councils); it studied only the four and says nothing of the connection of the other 31.
facts.system: Revenue Management Systems of the four city councils

facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study, dated August 2023, finds the four city councils have no comprehensive IT strategy and bring in systems piecemeal without working out what they need in infrastructure such as local internet connectivity, and that there was no national push or coordination behind the systems.
facts.system: City councils' office internet for cloud-based Revenue Management Systems

facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study reports that securing internet bandwidth at council offices, and connectivity for market point-of-sale devices (usually a mobile SIM card), was the responsibility of the city councils themselves and not of the software vendors, who run the revenue systems for 3 to 20 per cent of the revenue handled; the owner of the connection is the local authority, not a ministry.
facts.system: City councils' office internet for cloud-based Revenue Management Systems

The `owner:ministry` fact is forced by the closed list: the document makes the city council itself, a local authority, responsible for its own internet, and the parent should read it as 'the state, local'. facts.fact: The Nation reports a National Local Government Finance Committee presentation to a meeting with the Ministry of Local Government and councils in Mzuzu in the week before 22 September 2022 (the article's published date; the page is undated) as stating a lack of local authority IFMIS connectivity: the real-time network the government intended never happened, the council's local network links only the District Commissioner's or chief executive's office to the council's own data centre, most servers in many councils do not work properly and data is consolidated by hand.
facts.system: Local Authorities IFMIS network

facts.fact: The Nation reports the Malawi Local Government Association's executive director saying in September 2022 (the article's published date; the page is undated) that councils use the new central government IFMIS to process salary payments and nothing else yet, and that efforts to link the local IFMIS with the central one have produced nothing on the ground; the article does not say from where or over what connection councils reach the central system.
facts.system: Central government IFMIS, used by councils for salaries
